mainTopic: טובת הנאה in priestly gifts, and the leniencies of תרומת חוצה לארץ
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא which teaches that the owner of produce keeps טובת הנאה, the right to choose which כהן gets his תרומה. Another ישראל may pay him a סלע to send it to a grandson who is a כהן, but a כהן may not pay for his own gifts. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא leaves out מתנות כהונה because they have only קדושת דמים, so a payment might make people think they were redeemed and treat them as ordinary food. The גמרא then turns to תרומת חוצה לארץ, which is only a rabbinic obligation and so has many leniencies. רבא allows giving it to a כהן who helped at the threshing floor. שמואל says it is cancelled out by a simple majority, and stories about רבה and רב הונא show this rule in practice. שמואל also allows eating first and separating later, and he forbids it only to someone whose טומאה comes from his own body, and only for eating. רבינא draws a practical rule from this for a נדה separating חלה. The amud ends with a woman on a boat asking whether a טמא מת may immerse and eat this תרומה; רב נחמן's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner keeps the benefit of choosing who gets his gifts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the owners of the produce have טובת הנאה, the right to decide which כהן or לוי receives their gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The benefit of choosing belongs to the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא's rule: the owner of produce keeps the small benefit of choosing which כהן or לוי gets his gifts. The next step will explain what this means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts themselves belong to the כהנים as a group, but the owner decides which specific כהן receives them. That power to choose is a small benefit, and it is called טובת הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The small benefit of choosing who receives a gift
The owners (here, the owner of the produce)

phrases.english: The benefit of discretion belongs to the owners.
phrases.notes: He means the owner gets to pick which כהן or לוי receives his תרומה and מעשרות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner of produce has טובת הנאה over his תרומה and מעשרות.

steps.title: Example: paying a coin to direct the gift to a grandson
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא illustrates the rule. A ישראל may pay the owner a סלע so that the תרומה goes to his grandson the כהן, but a כהן may not pay to have the gifts go to another כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Suppose an Israelite separated תרומה from his pile of grain, and another Israelite came along and said to him: 'Take this סלע and give the תרומה to my daughter's son, who is a כהן.' This is permitted. If it was a כהן paying for the gifts to go to another כהן, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a concrete case of טובת הנאה: the owner's right to choose has real value, and another ישראל may pay him for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the owner controls who gets the תרומה, an outsider can 'buy' that choice for a coin and send the gift to a relative who is a כהן. When a כהן does the paying, though, it looks as if כהנים are buying the gifts that are supposed to come to them freely, so that is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an example)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A pile of grain
A coin worth four זוּזִים

steps.confusionAlert: The coin is not buying the תרומה itself; the תרומה still has to go to a כהן. The coin only pays for the owner's right to choose WHICH כהן gets it.
steps.whatToRemember: A ישראל may pay for the owner's choice, but a כהן may not pay to receive his priestly gifts.

phrases.english: How so?
An Israelite who separated תרומה from his pile of grain,
and another Israelite found him and said to him:
'Here, take this סלע for yourself,'
'and give it to my daughter's son, who is a כהן.' It is permitted.
If it was a כהן paying for another כהן, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of step 1 with a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל may pay the owner to send the תרומה to a particular כהן; a כהן may not pay for this.

steps.title: Why doesn't the ברייתא mention the priestly gifts from animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא only speaks about תרומה and does not also say that the owner has טובת הנאה in מתנות כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the תנא's reason for not mentioning the gifts of the priesthood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא limits its example to תרומה and leaves out מתנות כהונה. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מתנות כהונה are also gifts given to a כהן, so you might expect the same rule of choosing to apply to them. The ברייתא's silence about them suggests there is a reason they are different.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the ברייתא
What is the reason?
Priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal (foreleg, jaw, maw)

phrases.english: And the תנא, what is his reason
that he does not mention the gifts of the priesthood?
phrases.notes: These are the foreleg, jaw and maw that go to a כהן from every ordinary animal that is slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא's rule is limited to תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא says the owner has טובת הנאה in תרומה but does not say so about מתנות כהונה.

steps.title: תרומה is permanently holy, so nobody will be confused
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תרומה has קדושת הגוף and can never be redeemed, so taking money for the choice will not cause anyone to mistake it for ordinary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא would tell you: תרומה has holiness in its very body, and since it can never be redeemed, people will not come to make a mistake with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by explaining why money changing hands is safe in the case of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is holy in itself and can never be turned into ordinary food by redeeming it. Everyone knows this, so even if a coin is paid over it, nobody will think the coin removed its holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (the answer the תנא would give)
Holiness in the object itself, which cannot be redeemed
Can be redeemed (made ordinary)
To make a mistake

phrases.english: He would say to you:
תרומה, which has holiness in its very body,
since it cannot be redeemed,
people will not come to make a mistake with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With תרומה there is no risk of error, because its קדושת הגוף can never be redeemed.

steps.title: Priestly gifts could be mistaken for redeemed food
steps.stepSummary: מתנות כהונה have only קדושת דמים, so if money were paid for them, people might think their holiness was redeemed for four זוזים and treat them like ordinary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these gifts, since they have holiness tied to their value, people might make a mistake with them. They might say their holiness can be redeemed for four זוזים, and then come to treat them like ordinary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing why the ברייתא leaves out מתנות כהונה: with them, paying money could lead people into a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness of מתנות כהונה is קדושת דמים, which is tied to value, not to the object itself. If someone saw a סלע (four זוזים) paid over them, he might think the coin redeemed them and made them ordinary food. That is why the תנא mentions only תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness tied to value, which money can affect
זוּזִים, silver coins (four make a סֶלַע)
Ordinary, non-holy food
Manner of treatment

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא speaks only about תרומה because it can never be redeemed. מתנות כהונה, whose holiness is tied to value, might be mistaken for ordinary food if money were paid over them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the type of holiness (קדושת הגוף or קדושת דמים) decides whether a money deal might confuse people about an item's status.

phrases.english: These, since they have holiness tied to their value,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the מתנות כהונה from the question in step 3.

phrases.english: people will come to make a mistake with them,
thinking that their holiness can be redeemed for four זוזים,
and they will come to treat them the way one treats ordinary food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by contrasting מתנות כהונה with תרומה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מתנות כהונה are left out because their קדושת דמים could lead people to think a payment redeemed them, so they would treat the gifts as חולין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא limits טובת הנאה in its example to תרומה, which has קדושת הגוף, to prevent mistakes with מתנות כהונה.

steps.title: רבא: foreign תרומה may go to a כהן who helped
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the ban on a כהן המסייע בבית הגרנות does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל does not carry the problem of a כהן who helps out at the threshing floor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבא about תרומה grown outside ארץ ישראל. It is allowed to give it to a כהן who helped with the work at the threshing floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן may not help the farmer at the threshing floor in order to receive the gifts, because the gifts then look like wages for his work. Since תרומת חוצה לארץ is a lighter, rabbinic obligation, רבא says this concern does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה separated from produce grown outside ארץ ישראל, an obligation only from the Rabbis
A כהן who helps the owner with work in order to get the gifts
The threshing floors, where grain is processed and תרומה is separated

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying this produce is free of תרומה. It still needs תרומה. He is only saying that one specific restriction does not apply to it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Teruma from outside the Land [of Israel]
does not have in it [the problem] of
a priest who helps at the threshing floors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Related topic: how gifts may be given in exchange for benefit, now applied to תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on giving gifts to a כהן who helped at the threshing floor does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: רב חמא gives it to his servant
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא gave תרומת חוצה לארץ to his servant, a כהן, which shows רבא's rule in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא would give it to his attendant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing רבא's rule being followed. רב חמא gave this kind of תרומה to the כהן who served him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servant worked for רב חמא, so giving him תרומה looks like paying him for his service. רב חמא still did it, which fits רבא's rule that this concern does not apply to תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: An attendant, a personal helper
Gives

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama would give it to his attendant.
phrases.notes: The attendant was a כהן, and the 'it' here means תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא's ruling being acted on by an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the כהן המסייע restriction does not apply to תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב חמא, who gave such תרומה to his own attendant

steps.title: שמואל: foreign תרומה is nullified in a majority
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that תרומת חוצה לארץ that got mixed with ordinary food is cancelled out by a simple majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל is nullified in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second leniency, from שמואל. If this תרומה gets mixed into ordinary food, a simple majority of ordinary food is enough to cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular תרומה needs a hundred parts of ordinary food to be cancelled out. Because תרומת חוצה לארץ is only rabbinic, שמואל says a simple majority is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelled out in a majority; it loses its status when most of the mixture is ordinary food
Ordinary food that is not holy

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Teruma from outside the Land
is nullified in a majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ בְּטֵילָה בְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second leniency for תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified in a simple majority of ordinary food.

steps.title: רבה nullifies it on purpose and eats it while impure
steps.stepSummary: רבה would deliberately cancel out his תרומת חוצה לארץ in a majority and eat it even while he was טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would nullify it in a majority and eat it during his days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רבה, a כהן, used שמואל's rule. He mixed his foreign תרומה into a majority of ordinary food on purpose so that he could eat it even while he was טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With regular תרומה you may not cancel it out on purpose, and a טמא כהן may not eat it. רבה did both with תרומת חוצה לארץ, which shows how far its leniency goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels it out on purpose by mixing it into more ordinary food
The days when he was ritually impure

phrases.english: Rabba would nullify it in a majority,
and eat it during his days of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל's rule applied in practice, even in a stronger way.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified in a majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's practice of deliberately nullifying it and eating it while impure

steps.title: רב הונא's method for תרומה wine
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע mixed one jug of foreign תרומה wine into two jugs of ordinary wine, took one out, and then kept adding one and taking one out.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע happened to get תרומה wine, he would pour two jugs of ordinary wine and one jug of תרומה wine together and take one out. From then on, he would pour in one and take out one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story of using the majority rule. רב הונא set up a vat where the תרומה wine was always cancelled out by the ordinary wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two jugs of ordinary wine and one of תרומה, the ordinary wine is the majority, so the תרומה is cancelled out and he could drink a jug's worth. After that the vat stayed at two jugs, so each new jug of תרומה added was again outnumbered, and he could keep taking one out.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine
A jug or pitcher
Pours in, throws in
Takes out

steps.confusionAlert: He did not use new ordinary wine each time. The vat always held two jugs, so each new jug of תרומה was again outnumbered two to one.
steps.whatToRemember: תרומת חוצה לארץ is cancelled out by a simple majority, and the אמוראים relied on this in practice, even using it on purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua,
when he would happen to have teruma wine,
would pour two jugs of non-sacred [wine]
and one jug of teruma,
and take out one.
From here onward,
he would pour in one and take out one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כִּי מִתְרְמֵי לֵיהּ חַמְרָא דִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical story showing the majority rule for תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that תרומת חוצה לארץ is nullified in a majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ongoing method with a vat of wine

steps.title: שמואל: eat first, separate later
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that with produce from outside ארץ ישראל, one may eat first and separate the תרומה afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: with תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל, a person may go ahead and eat, and afterward separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more leniency from שמואל. A person may start eating produce from outside ארץ ישראל before separating its תרומה, and separate it later from what is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With produce grown in ארץ ישראל, eating anything before the תרומה is taken off is forbidden. For produce from outside ארץ ישראל, שמואל allows eating first, as long as the תרומה is separated afterward from the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes ahead and eats
Separates (the תרומה)

steps.whatToRemember: תרומת חוצה לארץ has several leniencies: it may go to a כהן who helped, it is cancelled out by a simple majority, and one may eat first and separate later.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
[Regarding] teruma from outside the Land,
one may proceed to eat,
and afterward separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּרוּמַת חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ אוֹכֵל וְהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further ruling of שמואל, adding another leniency for תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may eat produce from outside ארץ ישראל first and separate its תרומה afterward.

steps.title: Foreign תרומה is forbidden only to someone impure from his own body, and only for eating
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that תרומת חוצה לארץ is forbidden only to a person whose טומאה comes from his own body, and that this applies only to eating it, not to touching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: תרומה from outside the Land is forbidden only to a person whose impurity comes out of his own body. And this is only about eating it. But touching it is no problem for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another lenient ruling of שמואל about תרומת חוצה לארץ. It limits which kinds of טומאה make this תרומה forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a טומאה that comes from the person's own body (like a בעל קרי or a נדה) forbids eating this תרומה. A טומאה that came from outside, like touching a dead body, does not. Even a person impure from his own body may still touch it. The ban is only on eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose impurity comes out of his own body (like a בעל קרי or a נדה)
Eating
Touching
We have no problem with it

steps.whyThisMatters: This two-part limit (only body-based טומאה, only eating) is the base for רבינא's practical rule in the next step.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Teruma from outside the Land is not forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁהַטּוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: except to one whose impurity comes out upon him from his own body,
and this applies only to eating,
but as for touching, we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another of שמואל's leniencies for תרומת חוצה לארץ, this time about טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומת חוצה לארץ is forbidden only to one whose טומאה comes from his body, and only for eating. Touching is allowed.

steps.title: A נדה may separate חלה outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא applies שמואל's rule. A נדה may separate חלה, and a young כהן eats it. If there is no young כהן, she burns it, separates a second reminder piece, and an adult כהן eats that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore a נדה may separate חלה, and a young כהן eats it. If there is no young כהן, she picks it up on the tip of a skewer and throws it into the oven. Then she separates another piece as חלה, so that people do not forget the law of חלה, and an adult כהן eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא turns שמואל's rule into a practical guide for a woman who is a נדה and is baking outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since touching is fine, the נדה may separate the חלה herself. Since eating is forbidden only to someone impure from his body, a young כהן who never had such טומאה may eat it. If none is around, the first piece is burned, and a second piece is taken only to keep the law alive. An adult כהן may eat that second piece.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It marks a practical result drawn from an earlier rule.
Cuts off (separates) the חלה portion from the dough
A young כהן, too young to have had טומאה from his own body
A skewer or poker
The law and practice of חלה

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל does NOT mean the High Priest. It just means an adult כהן, the opposite of the כֹּהֵן קָטָן mentioned earlier.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside ארץ ישראל: a נדה may separate חלה, a young כהן may eat it, and if none is present the piece is burned. A second reminder piece is then given to an adult כהן.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore,
a menstruating woman may separate ḥalla,
and a minor priest eats it,
and if there is no minor priest,
she takes it on the tip of a skewer,
and throws it into the oven,
and then she separates another ḥalla,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח תּוֹרַת חַלָּה,
phrases.english: so that the law of ḥalla will not be forgotten,
and an adult priest eats it.
phrases.notes: "גדול" here just means grown-up, not the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result (הילכך) from שמואל's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה may separate חלה outside the Land. A young כהן eats it. If there is none, it is burned, and a second reminder piece is given to an adult כהן.

steps.title: A woman on a boat asks whether a טמא מת may immerse and eat foreign תרומה
steps.stepSummary: While רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רמי בר חמא are on a boat, a woman asks whether a טמא מת may immerse and then eat תרומת חוצה לארץ. רב נחמן begins speaking to רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן, רב עמרם and רמי בר חמא were traveling on a boat. רב עמרם went off to relieve himself. A certain woman came in before them and said to them: Someone who is impure from a dead body, may he immerse and eat תרומה from outside the Land? רב נחמן said to רמי בר חמא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story in which a woman asks a practical question about a טמא מת and foreign תרומה. The last line sets up רב נחמן's response, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת's טומאה came from outside, not from his own body, so it fits the lighter category from step 12. Her question is whether just immersing in a מקוה is enough for him to eat this תרומה. The answer has not been given yet; the story stops just as רב נחמן turns to רמי בר חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A boat or ferry
To relieve himself
